text: Let's meet the other real engine sharing OneLake — Fabric Warehouse.

A lakehouse is Spark-first, with a SQL endpoint bolted on. A Warehouse flips that — it's SQL-first, full T-SQL, the exact dialect this track's own T-SQL course covered. And its tables still live in the same OneLake, same Delta format underneath.

New item, Warehouse, name it, create — and it opens to a T-SQL editor, genuinely the same kind of interface the T-SQL course's SSMS lessons used. And unlike a lakehouse's read-only SQL endpoint, a Warehouse supports real inserts, updates, and full transactions.

This track actually started with a standalone T-SQL course. A Fabric Warehouse is where that entire skill set becomes directly relevant to real data engineering work — the same syntax, now against a lakehouse-adjacent warehouse table.
Same storage, a genuinely different engine on top. Next lesson: lakehouse versus warehouse, choosing the right one.
